adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — A collective cohost uses the first host's calendar ID with their own credentials, so Office365 creation fails or targets the wrong calendar instead of their destination (also affects Lark and CalDAV).

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the Office365CalendarService.ts diff, the createEvent method extracts `mainHostDestinationCalendar` from the first element of the destinationCalendar array and uses it to construct the eventsUrl. Unlike GoogleCalendarService which was updated to find the calendar matching the credentialId (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), Office365CalendarService simply takes the first calendar from the array. This means when there are multiple hosts with different destination calendars, all Office365 calendar services will use the first host's calendar ID rather than finding their own matching calendar. This is a real bug where collective cohosts would have events created in the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Cancelling all occurrences of a collective booking repeatedly deletes only the first reference with organizer credentials, leaving cohosts' newly created events active after the series is marked cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff around line 449 in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code iterates through bookingCalendarReference (now an array) with a for loop. However, inside the loop when handling recurring events with allRemainingBookings, the code still uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter((credential) => credential.type.endsWith('_calendar'))` which only processes the organizer's credentials, not the credentials associated with each specific reference in the outer loop. The outer loop variable `reference` with its `credentialId` is not being used in the recurring event deletion logic - instead it falls back to iterating all user calendar credentials. This means for collective bookings where cohosts have their own calendar references, only the organizer's calendar events would be deleted during recurring event cancellation, not the cohosts' events. This is a real bug in the refactored code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — Dropping credentialId from video references makes handleCancelBooking skip its credential-gated deleteMeeting call, leaving video meetings active after cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at line 170 in EventManager.ts, the code changes from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. For video references (when isCalendarType is false), the old code used `result.credentialId` but the new code uses `undefined`. This means video references will have `credentialId: undefined` instead of the actual credential ID. In handleCancelBooking.ts, the code checks `if (credentialId)` before calling deleteMeeting, so if credentialId is undefined, the video meeting deletion would be skipped. However, looking more carefully at the diff, for video types (isCalendarType is false), the old code was `result.credentialId` and new code is `undefined`. This is indeed a change that could cause video meetings to not be deleted. But I need to verify this is actually the case - the finding claims this affects video references specifically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171 — Changing destinationCalendar from an object/null to an array silently breaks webhook and integration consumers that parse the existing payload shape.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that destinationCalendar is being changed from a single object/null to an array throughout the codebase. This is evidenced by multiple changes in the diff: the webhook test file shows 'destinationCalendar: null' changing to 'destinationCalendar: []', the CalendarEventClass shows the type changing from 'DestinationCalendar | null' to 'DestinationCalendar[] | null', and numerous code changes show destructuring patterns like 'const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []'. This is a breaking change to the API/webhook payload structure that would affect external consumers who expect the old object shape. The diff in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts line 171 is not shown, but the evidence throughout the diff confirms this type change is happening and would break existing integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Google Meet bookings without a destination calendar dereference undefined and fail instead of falling back to Cal Video.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at line 119 in EventManager.ts: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is undefined or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`, and accessing `.integration` on `undefined` will throw a TypeError. The original code checked `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which safely handled the undefined case. This is a real bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:370 — Passing every host the full destination array makes Office365, Lark and CalDAV target the first host's calendar and fail to create other hosts' events.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the finding claims that passing the full destination array to all calendar services causes Office365, Lark, and CalDAV to target the first host's calendar. Examining the code: In EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents(), for each destination in event.destinationCalendar, it finds the credential matching destination.credentialId and calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId). The full event (with all destinationCalendar entries) is passed to each calendar service. Looking at Office365CalendarService.ts, it does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and uses only the first entry. Similarly, LarkCalendarService.ts does the same destructuring. This means when creating events for the second host, these services will still use the first host's destination calendar info, not the correct one for that credential. GoogleCalendarService correctly uses `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` to find the right calendar. So the finding is correct - Office365 and Lark will incorrectly use the first host's calendar for all hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:257 — Legacy references without externalCalendarId now resolve no calendar for updates instead of using the destination calendar, breaking rescheduling.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 253-255 in the diff: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. This is indeed problematic logic - when externalCalendarId is falsy (the else branch), the code tries to find a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but externalCalendarId is already falsy/undefined at that point, so this will never match anything. The same issue exists at line 314-316 for deleteEvent. Previously, the code would fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` which would work. Now it will always return undefined when externalCalendarId is not provided, breaking the fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148 — Destinations without credentialId no longer match any Google credential and silently create bookings on primary instead of the selected calendar.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts around line 148, the code changes from using `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly to using `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. The finding claims that destinations without credentialId will silently fall back to 'primary'. However, examining the code: (1) The createEvent method now receives a credentialId parameter, (2) It searches for a destination calendar matching that credentialId, (3) If not found, it falls back to 'primary' with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || 'primary'`. This is actually the intended behavior - if there's no matching destination calendar for this credential, using 'primary' is a reasonable fallback. The concern about 'destinations without credentialId' is not quite accurate - the credentialId comes from the credential being used to create the event, not from the destination calendar itself. The code correctly matches destination calendars to credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — Cancelling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes only organizer references and leaves cohost calendar events active.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff around line 449 in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code iterates through bookingCalendarReference (now an array) and for each reference with a credentialId, it finds the calendar credential and deletes events. However, in the recurring event deletion logic (lines 430-448), it still uses `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter((credential) => credential.type.endsWith('_calendar'))` which only looks at the organizer's credentials, not the credentials of all hosts. This means for collective bookings where multiple hosts have calendar references, only the organizer's calendar events would be deleted during recurring event cancellation. The outer loop processes each reference, but the inner recurring event logic doesn't use the specific credentialId from each reference - it just iterates over the user's own credentials. This is a real bug where cohost calendar events may not be properly deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — Requiring a database credential ID in every provider's createEvent contract leaks Google-specific destination lookup into the shared boundary, forcing unrelated providers and all future implementations to carry an argument they cannot use.

The finding assumes all providers must implement this parameter, but the diff shows only GoogleCalendarService has this change. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — The new credential lookup and manual CredentialWithAppName reconstruction is duplicated in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents, so changes to credential loading or required fields can silently diverge between create and update paths.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, there is indeed duplicated credential lookup logic in both createAllCalendarEvents (lines 344-365) and updateAllCalendarEvents (lines 505-526). Both sections fetch credentials from DB when not found in calendarCredentials, and both manually construct a CredentialWithAppName object with the same fields. This is a real code duplication issue that could lead to maintenance problems if the credential structure changes - one location might be updated while the other is forgotten. However, this is more of a code quality/maintainability concern rather than a bug or correctness issue. The code will function correctly, it's just not DRY. This is borderline - it's a real observation about the code structure, but whether it constitutes a 'problem' depends on standards. It's a valid code review finding about duplication that could cause future issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — The recurring-series deletion batch runs once per calendar reference, multiplying remote deletes by the reference count and causing severe latency and provider rate-limit pressure.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff around line 449, the code iterates through `bookingCalendarReference` (now an array) with `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside this loop, when handling recurring events, there's a nested loop that iterates through ALL user credentials with `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter((credential) => credential.type.endsWith('_calendar')).map(...)`. This means for each calendar reference, the code processes ALL calendar credentials and deletes events for ALL updated bookings. If there are multiple calendar references (e.g., 2), and multiple calendar credentials (e.g., 3), and multiple updated bookings (e.g., 10), this could result in 2 * 3 * 10 = 60 delete operations instead of the intended number. This is a real bug where the recurring deletion logic is incorrectly nested inside the per-reference loop, causing duplicate delete attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — Multi-host event creation serially awaits each host's credential lookup and calendar API call, making booking latency grow by the sum of every host's network latency.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in packages/core/EventManager.ts around line 339, the code does use a for...of loop with await inside: `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar) { ... const createdEvent = await createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId); ... }`. This is indeed serial execution rather than parallel. However, this is a performance concern/optimization suggestion rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness problem. The code will function correctly, just potentially slower for multi-host scenarios. The finding describes a real architectural choice that could impact performance, but it's not a defect - it's a design tradeoff. Serial execution might even be intentional to avoid race conditions or rate limiting issues with calendar APIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:504 — Updating a collective booking performs a serial credential query for every host reference missing from the organizer's credentials, creating an N+1 query path whose latency grows linearly with team size.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in packages/core/EventManager.ts around line 504, the code iterates through calendarReference array and for each reference, if credential is not found in this.calendarCredentials, it performs a prisma.credential.findUnique query. This is indeed an N+1 query pattern - for a team booking with N hosts, if their credentials aren't in the organizer's calendarCredentials, it will make N separate database queries sequentially (not batched). The same pattern exists in createAllCalendarEvents around line 347. This is a real performance issue that grows linearly with team size.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — Empty destination-calendar arrays make Google Meet booking creation throw before fallback processing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 119 in EventManager.ts, the code is `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. The variable `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is extracted from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` using array destructuring on line 117. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array `[]`, then `mainHostDestinationCalendar` will be `undefined`. Accessing `.integration` on `undefined` will throw a TypeError. This is a real bug - when destinationCalendar is an empty array (which is now the default as shown in the webhook test change from `null` to `[]`), the code will crash before reaching the fallback logic.
